newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania miners' boss blames riots on ex-communists.
newsitem.headline: Romania miners' boss blames riots on ex-communists.

text.p: Romanian miners' union leader Miron Cosma, on trial accused of undermining state authority, on Tuesday blamed ex-communists for 1991 riots which toppled the country's first reformist government.
On the second day of his trial, Cosma said ex-president Ion Iliescu and former prime minister Petre Roman had wanted the coalminers to come to Bucharest to press for a reshuffle.
"You would never put Petre Roman, now Senate chairman, or Mr. Iliescu, a former head of state, on trial," Cosma told Bucharest court judges. "Instead, you only put me on trial."
Cosma, 42, led thousands of miners on a three-day September 1991 rampage to Bucharest. Government offices were damaged and three people were killed during clashes with security forces.
Roman was forced to quit during those riots, which he subsequently blamed on a putsch by communists around Iliescu -- accusations Iliescu has publicly denied.
If found guilty of the charges, Cosma faces up to 15 years in jail. The court decided to resume the hearing on May 26 to hear evidence from some 360 witnesses.
Cosma has rejected the charges, ranging from undermining state authority to breaking firearms rules, and said he is a scapegoat in a political trail.
"Petty thieves are always jailed, whereas the big sharks are always allowed to go free," he said.
Many Romanians believe Cosma was not alone in organising the riots. Successive waves of political violence in 1990 culminated in the September 1991 anti-government rioting.

"Cosma is only a tool and he shouldn't be alone in the box," said Alexandru Stanciu, a retired army colonel who was among the audience in the court on Tuesday. "The miners are innocent, they are simple-minded people who were manipulated," he said.
